summary: Static code review of Souvera Shield v2.3.2 for the two preventive fixes (dual-group access + dual-group repair step) plus regression sweep. No PHP/Nextcloud runtime is available in the sandbox – review is source-inspection only. All acceptance criteria from the review request are satisfied. Only one cosmetic mismatch found (template footer version string). The most likely remaining cause of the reported 404 is that `occ upgrade` has not been executed on the target Nextcloud after uploading v2.3.2 – there is nothing further to fix in the code.

minor.issue: Footer displays 'v2.3.1' but /app/appinfo/info.xml is now 2.3.2 – cosmetic mismatch only, does NOT cause the 404. Change `v2.3.1` to `v2.3.2` to align.

Docblock (lines 22-24) claims that `ProviderToolsClient` service is registered, but register() does not call registerService() for it. It works today because Nextcloud's DI autowires classes with typed constructor deps – this is a documentation drift, not a runtime bug. Either add the explicit service factory (mirror the PMGClient block) or delete the doc line.
Leftover from iteration_1: DmarcDomainMapper::findActive() is still defined but no longer referenced anywhere (dead code).

action_items: USER-SIDE FIX (very likely the 404 cause): run `sudo -u www-data php occ upgrade` on the target Nextcloud after uploading v2.3.2. Until upgrade completes, NC keeps the app in 'needs upgrade' state and every route (incl. /apps/souvera_shield/) returns 404 regardless of group membership. Then verify with `occ app:list | grep souvera_shield` (should list 2.3.2 under Enabled) and `occ config:app:get souvera_shield enabled` (should be 'yes' or a JSON array containing both groups).
OPTIONAL: bump the template footer /app/templates/main.php line 325 from 'v2.3.1' to 'v2.3.2' to match info.xml.
OPTIONAL: register ProviderToolsClient explicitly in Application::register() or remove the doc line that claims it is registered.
OPTIONAL: delete unused DmarcDomainMapper::findActive() (dead code, flagged already in iteration_1).

hypothesis_ranking: H1 (highest probability): `occ upgrade` was not executed after uploading v2.3.2. Nextcloud stores the last-run app version in oc_appconfig (souvera_shield.installed_version). When info.xml <version> is higher than the stored value, NC flags the app as 'needs upgrade' and 404s every route (both page and REST) until the upgrade sequence runs the DB migrations + repair steps. This is a standard NC behaviour, unrelated to group membership. Verification on the user's server: `occ config:app:get souvera_shield installed_version` — if it shows 2.3.1 while info.xml says 2.3.2, this is the cause. Run `occ upgrade` (or `occ app:enable --force souvera_shield` won't help; upgrade is the correct command).
H2 (second): stale app cache. NC caches app metadata in oc_appconfig / opcache. After `occ upgrade` also run `occ maintenance:repair` and clear opcache (or restart php-fpm).
H3 (third): if v2.3.1 already deployed successfully and only the two touched files were uploaded for v2.3.2, but info.xml version was bumped — same root cause as H1: the upgrade sequence has not run.

H4 (very unlikely, ruled out by code review): PHP fatal during boot. Ruled out because (a) all `use` statements resolve to existing classes, (b) no removed classes still referenced, (c) every route name maps to an existing controller method, (d) no invalid Doctrine types or oversized index names in migrations.
root_cause_analysis_for_the_404.conclusion: The two code fixes (FIX-A dual-group access + FIX-B dual-group repair step) are correctly implemented and will take effect once `occ upgrade` is executed on the target server. There is no additional latent code bug to blame – proceed with the upgrade step and, if 404 persists after `occ upgrade` completes without errors, capture the output of `occ app:list | grep souvera_shield`, `occ config:app:get souvera_shield installed_version`, and `occ config:app:get souvera_shield enabled` and report back.
